advice: Propose a fused 16×16 A-tile transpose and compute path for n=512. For each 32-row output band and 32-column B panel, take A tiles with `a_tile[q,i] = A[(r+i)*512 + k+q]` for `i,q=0..15`. Load the row-major tile into SVE vectors, transpose it with vector zip/unzip operations, then feed its 16 column vectors and the matching B values to the existing FP32 MOPA accumulator. Keep the output accumulator in ZA across all 512 K values; do not use ZA for the input transpose. Write C with the existing stores. Use original A and B, keep the NN ABI and fallback, and do not add persistent storage. The hypothesis is that removing full A-stack packing and its later reads may offset the repeated small-tile transpose work. This is unverified. There are 16 column panels, so this recomputes the transpose of every A element 16 times: 4,194,304 FP32 elements (16 MiB read and 16 MiB of transposed values produced) versus one full A pass of 262,144 elements (1 MiB) in the existing packing path. Count all tile loads, vector shuffles, allocation, and stores in the timed call.
risks: The 16-fold repeated transpose work may cost more than the removed full-buffer packing. SVE transpose shuffles and register pressure may also slow the MOPA loop or require spills; spills could erase the expected benefit. Preserve each output's K accumulation order and FP32 arithmetic. Validate fresh inputs against the frozen tolerance, full C overwrite, n=512, general sizes and tails, n<=0, and allocation-failure behavior. Inspect compiler output for unintended spills and verify that no external library or state persists between calls. If measured, use ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls, retain each report's best-of-three timing, report spread and both historical and fresh same-mode peak comparisons, and apply the unchanged adoption gate and held-out check. Do not infer an isolated transpose cost or causal benefit from whole-call scores.
